title: Why Disability Belongs in Every Climate Conversation

body.en: When the last flood warning went out, it reached radios, phone screens, and loudspeaker announcements moving through the streets. For most people, that was enough. For Kwabena, who is Deaf, none of those channels reached him at all — he found out the water was rising when it was already at his doorstep. This isn't a story about Kwabena being vulnerable. It's a story about a warning system built for one kind of person. Around 15% of any population lives with some form of disability, and climate risks — heat, flooding, storms — don't skip anyone. Planning that only works for some people isn't complete planning. It's a gap with a name.

followUpQuestion: Why didn't the flood warning actually reach Kwabena, even though it was broadcast?
